metadata.title: Self-Check Isn't Verification.
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: a self-check can only confirm what it already believes; verification means checking against a source the agent never wrote. Lands the carry-out via the source's five-claim worked example — a tampered citation still passes self-check, and only opening the actual paper catches it.
metadata.anchor_pair: B01 -> B06 (the five-claim self-check table: planted with the first clean pass, returns with the outside check added and the planted error caught)

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes that when Claude checks its own answer and calls it verified, that's final. But self-check is only a first pass — so: is a self-check verification, or just a first pass?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Claude checked its own answer. It says verified. That's final. Right?', hesitates on 'final', corrects to 'a first pass'

props.text:
Claude checked its own answer.
It says verified.
That's final.
Right?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. Single-word trigger ('final') swapped for a multi-word replacement phrase ('a first pass') mirroring the source's own B08 phrase. TIMING LAW: 32-word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('final' -> 'a first pass') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: Ask Claude for a five-claim research summary, one citation per claim — then ask it to self-check each claim against the source it just cited. The first pass comes back clean: all five, verified.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR - a five-row claim table, self-check column, all rows verified

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR - five claims, first pass clean
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. A five-row table appears one row at a time: CLAIM 1 through CLAIM 5, each gaining a SELF-CHECK column value of 'verified' in turn. THIS EXACT FIVE-ROW COMPOSITION RETURNS AT B06.

beats.narration_text: That looks like verification. The agent read the sources, wrote the claims, and checked its own work — three passes over the same material, all coming back clean.

shot.new_visual_element: Three passes looping over the same document, closing on a VERIFIED stamp

production_viz.label: The natural guess - three passes, all clean
production_viz.mechanic: A document icon labeled 'the summary' with three curved loop-arrows drawn around it in sequence, each labeled READ / WRITE / SELF-CHECK. The loop closes with a large stamp reading VERIFIED landing on top.

beats.narration_text: Now swap claim three's citation for a paper that doesn't actually support it, and run the self-check again. It still comes back verified — because the check reasons from the same claim it's supposed to be testing, not from the paper itself.

shot.new_visual_element: The tampered claim's row; the self-check loop closes over it and still stamps verified

production_viz.label: The break - the swap still passes
production_viz.mechanic: The CLAIM 3 row from B01 reappears, its citation crossed out in terracotta and replaced with a new one. The same self-check loop from B02 closes around this single row and stamps it VERIFIED again, unchanged.

beats.narration_text: Open the actual paper and the mismatch is immediate — the citation doesn't say what the claim says it says. That's independent verification: evidence from outside the agent's own reasoning, not another pass over the same one.

shot.new_visual_element: The self-check loop struck through; a separate actual-paper icon flags the row unsupported

production_viz.label: The independent check - outside the loop
production_viz.mechanic: The B03 self-check loop reappears, now struck through in terracotta. Beside it, physically separated with no arrow connecting them, a document icon labeled 'THE ACTUAL PAPER' — opening it flags the claim 3 row 'UNSUPPORTED' in terracotta.

beats.narration_text: Catching this one wrong citation doesn't mean every claim got the same scrutiny — the check proves the citation matches the claim, not that the paper's underlying finding is solid.

shot.new_visual_element: A checked boundary around 'citation matches claim'; a faded box outside reading 'finding itself is solid'

production_viz.label: A pass only proves what it checks
production_viz.mechanic: A dashed bounded box labeled 'CHECKED: citation matches claim' with a checkmark inside it. Outside the box's dashed boundary, a separate faded card reads 'finding itself is solid' with no checkmark — visibly untouched by the check.

beats.narration_text: And a clean self-check elsewhere isn't proof those claims are safe either — the same five-row table, checked for real: claims one, two, four, and five hold up under an outside check too. Only the planted error needed independent eyes to catch.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS - the same five-row table, human-check column added, four rows agree, row three diverges

production_viz.label: The anchor returns - checked for real
production_viz.mechanic: THE B01 FIVE-ROW TABLE RETURNS, identical layout. A HUMAN-CHECK column fills in beside SELF-CHECK, one row at a time: rows 1, 2, 4, 5 both read 'verified'; row 3 reads self-check 'verified' but human-check 'UNSUPPORTED' in terracotta, visibly diverging from the rest.

beats.narration_text: A self-check can only confirm what it already believes — verification means checking against a source the agent never wrote.

props.quote: A self-check can only confirm what it already believes — verification means checking against a source the agent never wrote.
props.sparkLine: It confirms what it already believes.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Give me an output where you cite a source for every claim you make. Then self-check each claim against what you just wrote. After that, I'll open the actual sources myself and compare: what did your self-check catch, what did it miss, and why did the miss happen? Liam, in for Bear.
